hints.title: Find the two-triangle condition geometrically
hints.body: Drop a perpendicular from the free endpoint of side b to the ray along the base. Its height is h=bsin30∘=b/2. A radius-a arc meets the forward base ray twice only when h<a<b.
hints.recap: Two possible triangles occur when the opposite side is longer than the altitude but shorter than the adjacent side.
hints.pitfall: At <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></math> the arc is tangent, giving one triangle; at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi></mrow></math> one proposed triangle collapses.

hints.title: Combine the strict bounds
hints.body: Substitute the actual side expressions into the strict two-triangle condition. Use the positive-length domain before cancelling any common factor, then solve both inequalities together.

hints.pitfall: The inequality directions stay unchanged because the cancelled factor is positive.

solution:
Positivity gives 1<x<5. Let a=x−1 be the side opposite 30∘, and let b=(x−1)(5−x) be the other given side. The perpendicular height to the base ray is b/2.

Two non-congruent triangles require b/2<a<b. Dividing by x−1>0 gives (5−x)/2<1<5−x. The left inequality gives x>3 and the right gives x<4.

Thus 3<x<4, which also satisfies the length domain: D. Both endpoints give only one nondegenerate configuration.
